mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, keep the signed subtraction order on both sides (e.g., (A - B) = (C - D)).
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence sets one signed difference equal to another.
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D|, losing the sign information.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable’s numeric value becomes known, immediately substitute it into every pending equation.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any direct count, transfer, or derived equation yields a concrete value for a variable.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known value unused in other equations, causing an under‑determined system.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, i.e., after any earlier transfers, direct counts, or overrides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any sentence of the form “A has K more (or fewer) than B” that appears after previous statements.
mathgap.example: Using the final value of B after later transfers when evaluating an earlier “A has K more than B” statement.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the query, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem asks for a specific person's count and the narrative contains many extraneous relationships.
mathgap.example: Including unrelated variables in the solving process, which adds unnecessary complexity and can lead to mistakes.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique capitalized token as a separate variable, even if two names differ by only a single letter.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever parsing the list of people, ensure that similarly‑spelled names are not merged.
mathgap.example: Merging “Jon” and “John” into one variable, causing contradictory equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret phrases like “the difference between the number of X that A and B have” as the signed subtraction A - B, preserving the order of the names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes a difference between two people's counts using the wording “difference between … A and B”.
mathgap.example: Treating “the difference between A and B” as |A - B| instead of A - B, losing the sign.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Translate “A has K more (fewer) items than B” into the signed equation A - B = K (or A - B = ‑K for fewer).
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any comparative sentence containing “more” or “fewer”.
mathgap.example: Writing A = B + K without keeping the subtraction form, which can cause sign errors in later equations.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says “X has N items”, assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count appears, especially if it occurs later in the narrative after earlier information about X.
mathgap.example: Treating a later “X has N” as an initial count and ignoring earlier overrides, leading to contradictory values.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application (Bidirectional)
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement ‘X gives K items to Y’ appears, immediately subtract K from X and add K to Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any sentence describing a transfer of items from one person to another.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction of a transfer or applying it after later statements, which mis‑adjusts the counts.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Difference Equality Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two signed differences (e.g., "(A - B) = (C - D)"), evaluate the equality using the current values of A, B, C, D at the point the statement appears, after processing any earlier transfers, direct counts, or overrides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any sentence of the form “The number of tomatoes that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of tomatoes that A and B have” (or similar).
mathgap.example: Treating the equality as a static equation using final values, ignoring a transfer that occurred earlier in the narrative.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model mistakenly interprets "A has K more than B" as B - A = K, reversing the intended subtraction.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always translate "A has K more than B" into the signed equation A - B = K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops the sign when processing difference statements, using |A - B| instead of A - B.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the sign of the subtraction; do not take absolute values.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model evaluates later comparative statements using counts before earlier transfers have been applied, or applies transfers out of order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, and use the updated counts for any subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes a direct count is always the starting value, ignoring later overrides that may redefine the count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, overwrite any previous value for that person at that point in the narrative.

mathgap.description: Ignoring chronological order when evaluating difference equality statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats all equations as simultaneous constraints and substitutes final variable values, overlooking that the equality was stated before later transfers or overrides.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing a difference equality, first apply all prior statements (counts, transfers, overrides) and then evaluate the equality using those intermediate values.
